case_description: User-defined equal-area 50-km cell not aligned to FIA administrative domains
factual_conclusion: Official FIA theory supports user-defined populations such as GIS polygons as domain d applied across all parent estimation units. Basic domain estimation does not require rebuilding Phase-1 strata for the cell. However, official variance must use parent stratum/EU design quantities, public plot coordinates are perturbed/swapped, and small-cell precision may be poor.
caveat_or_requirement: Do not treat public-coordinate membership as exact truth. Do not drop parent-design zero-domain plots from variance calculation.

case_description: 50-km cell wholly inside one State
factual_conclusion: Can be treated as a domain across all estimation units intersecting/covering the State-side area under one coherent State evaluation. Sum EU contributions and variances. Exact public-coordinate assignment and sample size remain caveats.
caveat_or_requirement: A coherent State EVALID/evaluation is required.

case_description: One cell crosses State boundary
factual_conclusion: Estimation units cannot cross States, but FIA explicitly sums independent EU/State estimates. A design-consistent construction is therefore piecewise State-domain totals, each under its coherent State design, then sum totals and variances.
caveat_or_requirement: If State evaluation vintages differ, temporal comparability becomes a separate design choice.

case_description: Cell cuts more than one FIA estimation unit
factual_conclusion: Official method forms domain estimates within each estimation unit and sums across independent units. User generally does not see this internal decomposition in EVALIDator/DATIM.
caveat_or_requirement: The domain indicator must be applied in every relevant EU.

case_description: Cell cuts multiple poststrata
factual_conclusion: This is normal domain estimation. Keep parent stratum weights W_h and plot sample sizes n_h; plot-level response is zero outside the domain. Cell-specific re-stratification is not required for the basic domain estimator.
caveat_or_requirement: Rebuilding poststrata at cell scale is an optional area-control approach, not a prerequisite for basic domain estimation.

case_description: Cell contains forest and nonforest land
factual_conclusion: FIA target population includes all land/water. For tree totals, nonforest plots/conditions contribute zero tree response. This is compatible with domain estimation. Trees per forest acre is a different ratio target.
caveat_or_requirement: Do not silently condition the sampling frame on forest only unless estimating a forest-land ratio/domain.

case_description: Cell has very few FIA plots
factual_conclusion: Estimator can be formally computed, but direct design-based precision may be poor and variance unstable. FIA literature gives minimum-sample guidance for tested variables, not a universal 50-km/species threshold.
caveat_or_requirement: Future bounded diagnostics must set a precision/sample-size gate; D09 does not choose one.

case_description: An EU intersecting the geographic cell has no plots classified in domain
factual_conclusion: Official 2022 documentation states estimation units with no plots containing domain d contribute zero to estimate and variance.
caveat_or_requirement: For a genuinely nonzero small domain this can still produce an uninformative zero estimate; this is a precision/small-area limitation, not proof the domain is empty.

case_description: Select public plots whose coordinates fall in cell and sum TPA_UNADJ×ADJ×EXPNS
factual_conclusion: For a coherent parent evaluation, the point-total algebra can be represented as a domain indicator, so zero-domain plots do not change the sum. But the approach is incomplete if it discards parent design information; it is not sufficient for official domain variance, and public-coordinate fuzzing/swapping makes exact cell membership uncertain.
caveat_or_requirement: Point estimate equivalence is conditional; official uncertainty requires full design bookkeeping.

case_description: Compute variance only from selected in-cell plots and their existing weights
factual_conclusion: Official domain variance uses parent n, n_h, W_h and zeros outside domain. Appendix 1 shows expansion-factor shortcut variance can be materially inaccurate (example 2.5× difference).
caveat_or_requirement: Do not infer variance from the selected subset alone.

case_description: Recalculate Phase-1/poststrat area information specifically for each 50-km cell
factual_conclusion: Not required for the basic official domain estimator. It is the first/preferred option when the cell itself is to be an area-controlled population, provided adequate sample size. A known-domain-area ratio approach is another official area-control option.
caveat_or_requirement: Mainline must decide whether Q1 needs basic domain total or explicit cell area control.

case_description: Assign plots to exact 50-km cells using public FIADB LAT/LON
factual_conclusion: Public coordinates are deliberately perturbed and some private plots are swapped. Exact FIA plot coordinates are confidential.
caveat_or_requirement: Approximate-domain analysis may be possible, but exact membership requires a spatial-data strategy decided by mainline.

case_description: Sum cell portion in State 1 + cell portion in State 2 + ...
factual_conclusion: FIA estimation units are confined to States and considered independent; totals and variances are summed across EUs and States.
caveat_or_requirement: Each State-side estimate must use its own coherent evaluation/design metadata.

case_description: Treat all measurements with calendar years 2017–2023 as one national official FIA evaluation
factual_conclusion: Current EVALID table proves State evaluation windows differ: some 2023 evaluations are 2017–2023, others 2016–2023, 2013–2023, 2014–2023, etc. An arbitrary calendar subset is not itself one FIA evaluation.
caveat_or_requirement: Raw MEASYEAR/calendar filtering can break coherence between sample membership and expansion/restratification metadata.

case_description: Use an official State EVALID whose member years are exactly 2017–2023
factual_conclusion: Where such an EVALID exists (e.g. Delaware 102023, West Virginia 542023), it is a coherent official evaluation for that State.
caveat_or_requirement: This does not solve States whose official evaluation window differs.

case_description: Combine plot records/panels while attaching weights from differing evaluation vintages
factual_conclusion: Poststratification is repeated when panels are added; panel combination may require method modification. Weights/strata must belong to one coherent design object.
caveat_or_requirement: A custom calendar-window estimator would require an explicitly reconstructed design, not silent weight mixing.

case_description: Use only A-fold (~half plots) but retain official full-evaluation EXPNS/weights unchanged
factual_conclusion: Full-sample weights encode full-sample inclusion/effective n. FIA-specific weight literature states changing effective sample size requires changing sampling weights. Under independent 50% thinning, naive unchanged-weight total is expected to be about half the full-sample total (inference).
caveat_or_requirement: Exact Q1 fold recalibration method is not specified by core FIA manuals.

case_description: Use only B-fold (~half plots) but retain official full-evaluation EXPNS/weights unchanged
factual_conclusion: Same reasoning as A-fold.
caveat_or_requirement: Requires fold-specific design treatment.

case_description: Treat A/B as a known second-phase probability sample and recalculate effective stratum sample sizes/weights and variance
factual_conclusion: General design-based logic and FIA-specific weight-adjustment literature support recalibration when effective inclusion probabilities change, but no official FIA core recipe for Q1-style A/B half-sample cross-fitting was found.
caveat_or_requirement: Future bounded statistical-design test required. Any split-block rule (State×EVALID×EU×stratum×panel) is an inference to preserve balance, not an FIA-prescribed method.

case_description: Assume missing factor 2 cancels after within-species normalization
factual_conclusion: Mathematically true only if the missing factor is exactly constant across all cells for that species/fold and support is unchanged. Random cell/stratum-specific fold retention violates that guarantee; variance never cancels.
caveat_or_requirement: Do not use cancellation as justification for unrecalibrated design weights.
